survey: A cartoon three-masted sailing ship in water, seen in a three-quarter view from slightly above and to the side. The stern is on the left and the bow points right and a little away from the viewer. Hull: a rounded wooden hull drawn from slightly above, so the inside of the stern deck shows over the near rail. Its planks curve along the hull and narrow toward the bow, and the rail sweeps up to the bow consistently. Two portholes sit low on the near side. They are near-circular, which suits a side that faces the camera almost directly. Masts: three vertical masts rise from inside the hull and stay parallel. Each has horizontal yards carrying billowed white square sails, and a small round crow's-nest disc on the main mast is seen slightly from below/edge-on, as expected near eye level. A rope ladder runs from the deck up to the mast. Bow: two spars angle up and forward from the bow, and a rope runs from the main masthead to the tip of the upper spar. Water: a flat sea with wave crests drawn from the same slightly raised viewpoint. The hull sits level in it with a splash and a reflection at the waterline, so contact agrees with the ground plane. The sails face the viewer more squarely than a real ship's would at this hull angle. That is a common stylized convention for ships, and the yards and masts stay mutually consistent, so it falls within acceptable stylization. All parts agree on one camera.
